what_its_for: Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives. It is also used to help you fall asleep (short-term sleep aid) and to treat mild symptoms of motion sickness, such as nausea and dizziness.
how_to_take: Take diphenhydramine exactly as directed on the package label or as your doctor tells you. Swallow tablets or capsules whole with a full glass of water. You may take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. If you are using the liquid form, measure your dose carefully with the measuring cup or spoon provided — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Do not take more than the recommended amount.
dosing: For adults and children 12 years and older: The usual dose is 25 to 50 mg every 4 to 6 hours for allergies. For sleep, take 50 mg at bedtime. Do not take more than 300 mg in 24 hours. For children 6 to 11 years old: The usual dose is 12.5 to 25 mg every 4 to 6 hours, but always check the package label and ask your doctor or pharmacist first. Do not give this medicine to children under 6 years old unless your doctor specifically tells you to.
missed_dose: If you are taking this medicine on a regular schedule and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store diphenhydramine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking diphenhydramine — it can greatly increase drowsiness and dizziness, which can be dangerous. Do not drive a car, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills, anxiety medications, muscle relaxers, or narcotic pain medicines, unless your doctor approves. Avoid taking other allergy or cold medicines that may also contain diphenhydramine to prevent accidental overdose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: difficulty urinating or cannot urinate at all, confusion or severe dizziness, fast or irregular heartbeat, difficulty breathing or tightness in your chest, severe allergic reaction (swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat), or if your symptoms do not improve after 7 days. Seek emergency help immediately if you take too much — overdose can be very serious.
when_it_works: Diphenhydramine usually starts working within 15 to 30 minutes after you take it. Its effects generally last 4 to 6 hours. For sleep, it typically makes you feel drowsy within 30 minutes. Remember that this medicine is only meant for short-term use — do not use it for more than 2 weeks for sleep without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Use with extra caution. Diphenhydramine can cause increased confusion, dizziness, and a higher risk of falls in older people. Many healthcare providers recommend that older adults avoid this medicine if possible. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using diphenhydramine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Children under 6 years: Do not use without a doctor's guidance. People with certain health conditions: Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, enlarged prostate, breathing problems (such as asthma or COPD), liver disease, or difficulty urinating, as this medicine may worsen these conditions.
